subject: general
question: Simple interest on a certain sum is one-fourth of the sum and the interest rate percentage per annum is 4 times the number of years. If the rate of interest increases by 2%, then what will be the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹5,000 for 3 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let, Amount = 1 then simple interest = 1/4

The rate of interest = R then, time = R/4 years

Now, 1/4 = [1 × R × (R/4)]/100

⇒ 1/4 = R2/400

⇒ R2 = 100

⇒ R = √100 = 10%

∴ The rate of interest = 10%

The new rate of interest = 10 + 2 = 12%

Total interest for 3 years = 3 × 12 = 36%

∴ The total simple interest = (36/100) × 5000 = 1800

∴ The simple interest (in ₹) is ₹1800

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The simple interest = one-fourth of the sum

The rate of interest = 4 times the number of years

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (p × r × t)/100

Where, p = The sum of the amount

r = Rate of interest

t = Time (years)

**Calculation:**

Let, the sum of the amount = P

The rate of interest = R%

So, the time = R/4 years

Then, P/4 = [P × R × (R/4)]/100

⇒ P/4 = (P × R × R)/400

⇒ 1 = R²/100

⇒ R2 = 100

⇒ R = √100 = 10%

∴ The rate of interest = 10%

The new rate of interest = 10 + 2 = 12%

Now, the simple interest = (5000 × 12 × 3)/100 = 1800

**∴ The simple interest (in ₹) is ₹1800**
